To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the T cell repertoire includes cells that are able to recognize the association of two different conventional antigens, and (ii) these cells are restricted to the H-2 haplotype of the donor of the conventional antigens.
the T cell receptor for antigen can be shared between two different H-2-restriction elements.

(1) T cell receptors specific for one self H-2 antigen can recognize a different self H-2 plus a conventional antigen X; (2) T cell receptors recognizing one H-2 plus X can recognize a different H- 2 plus a second conventional antigen, Y; and (3) the recognition of one H- 2 antigen plus a conventional antigen is influenced by the presence or absence of other self H-2 antigems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for the recognition of foreign antigens by T lymphocytes.
the analysis of the T cell antigen receptor repertoire and the recognition of antigen by the T cell receptor.
the molecular mechanisms that govern the recognition of foreign antigens by the immune system and the influence of self on the development of the T cell repertoire.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
H-2-restriction is a function of the H-2 molecule, and the H-2 molecules of a particular haplotype can be recognized by a given T cell receptor in association with different conventional antigens.
the T cell receptor is not specific for the antigenic complex as a whole but for the individual components of the complex.

the H-2 molecule is the primary target in the generation of the anti-minor T cell repertoire, but the minor histocompatibility antigen is the final target in the effector phase of the immune response.

the H-2 restriction element of a CTL population is not necessarily the H-2 type expressed by the responding cells.
the T cell receptor is a complex structure that can recognize a number of different antigenic complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire of a normal mouse can recognize a large variety of different antigenic complexes, including those formed by self H-2 plus minor H antigents and those formed by self and allogenic H-2 plus foreign antigens.
a single T cell receptor can bind to different H-2 antigends in association with different minor H antigends.
the T cell receptor is a highly plastic molecule capable of binding a wide variety of ligand structures.
